rows.source: HM Land Registry Practice Guide 40 supplements 3, 4 and 5
rows.check: Treat the great majority of registered title boundaries as general boundaries unless explicitly determined.

rows.source: HM Land Registry Practice Guide 40 supplements 3, 4 and 5
rows.check: Do not assign a standard tolerance, measurement or ratio between a general title-plan boundary and the legal boundary.

rows.source: HM Land Registry Practice Guide 40 supplements 3, 4 and 5
rows.check: Do not infer the precise legal boundary solely from the mapped physical feature position.

rows.source: HM Land Registry Practice Guide 40 supplements 3, 4 and 5
rows.check: Account for survey tolerances even when modern high-accuracy survey instruments are used.

rows.source: HM Land Registry Practice Guide 40 supplements 3, 4 and 5
rows.check: Require determined-boundary evidence before treating a boundary line as exact for registration purposes.

rows.source: HM Land Registry Practice Guide 40 supplements 3, 4 and 5
rows.check: For determined-boundary plans using measurements, require stated measurement accuracy of +/-10 mm.

rows.source: HM Land Registry Practice Guide 40 supplements 3, 4 and 5
rows.check: For determined-boundary measurements, require horizontal measurements rather than measurements taken along a slope.

rows.source: HM Land Registry Practice Guide 40 supplements 3, 4 and 5
rows.check: For determined-boundary measurements, require ties from at least two defined permanent physical features.

rows.source: HM Land Registry Practice Guide 40 supplements 3, 4 and 5
rows.check: Treat permanent reference features as features reasonably expected to remain in position for at least 10 years.

rows.source: HM Land Registry Practice Guide 40 supplements 3, 4 and 5
rows.check: Recognise typical title-plan scales of 1:1250 urban and 1:2500 rural as display scales, not a licence to derive exact boundaries.

rows.source: HM Land Registry Practice Guide 40 supplements 3, 4 and 5
rows.check: Require title plans to be interpreted together with the register and any filed documents referred to by the register.

rows.source: HM Land Registry Practice Guide 40 supplements 3, 4 and 5
rows.check: Do not convert title-plan dimensions or red edging into parcel elevation sample coordinates without an independent geometry-quality gate.

rows.source: Ordnance Survey OS Terrain 5 official product documentation
rows.check: Treat OS Terrain 5 as a digital terrain model of the ground surface with protruding features such as buildings and trees removed.

rows.source: Ordnance Survey OS Terrain 5 official product documentation
rows.check: Use the 5 m grid post spacing as the product sampling resolution; do not represent it as sub-metre LiDAR.

rows.source: Ordnance Survey OS Terrain 5 official product documentation
rows.check: Treat 5 m contour intervals as contour representation, not per-parcel vertical precision.

rows.source: Ordnance Survey OS Terrain 5 official product documentation
rows.check: Require British National Grid / EPSG:27700 consistency before joining OS Terrain 5 geometry to parcel geometry.

rows.source: Ordnance Survey OS Terrain 5 official product documentation
rows.check: Record the product's quarterly update cadence when assessing source freshness.

rows.source: Ordnance Survey OS Terrain 5 official product documentation
rows.check: Track 5 km by 5 km tile identity so elevation samples can be reproduced to a specific supply tile.

rows.source: Ordnance Survey OS Terrain 5 official product documentation
rows.check: Record per-tile metadata rather than assuming one national metadata record is sufficient.

rows.source: Ordnance Survey OS Terrain 5 official product documentation
rows.check: Keep grid and contour representations separate because both derive from the same source but encode elevation differently.

rows.source: Ordnance Survey OS Terrain 5 official product documentation
rows.check: Use the published urban and major-route accuracy figure of 1.5 m RMSE as an uncertainty guard, not as a correction value.

rows.source: Ordnance Survey OS Terrain 5 official product documentation
rows.check: Use the published rural accuracy figure of 2.5 m RMSE as an uncertainty guard, not as a correction value.

rows.source: Ordnance Survey OS Terrain 5 official product documentation
rows.check: Use the published mountain/moorland accuracy figure of 2.5 m RMSE as an uncertainty guard, not as a correction value.

rows.source: Ordnance Survey OS Terrain 5 official product documentation
rows.check: Do not promote a parcel height-difference result from OS Terrain 5 until tile, CRS, vertical reference and sample reproducibility evidence are all present.

rows.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
rows.check: Prefer the Environment Agency 1 m composite DTM for England where parcel coverage is available because it is a terrain model rather than a surface-object model.

rows.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
rows.check: Record the nominal 1 m spatial resolution separately from vertical accuracy.

rows.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
rows.check: Record that the 2022 composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.

rows.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
rows.check: When repeated surveys exist, require provenance showing which newest/best-resolution survey was selected for the location.

rows.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
rows.check: Record bilinear interpolation as a lineage flag wherever source data was resampled before merging.

rows.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
rows.check: Require metadata-index lookup for the exact survey used at each sampled location.

rows.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
rows.check: Require GeoTIFF tile identity and 5 km tile alignment to the OS National Grid for reproducible sampling.

rows.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
rows.check: Require elevations to be interpreted in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.

rows.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
rows.check: Require OSTN15 transformation compatibility before combining parcel coordinates with the composite.

rows.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
rows.check: Use the published +/-15 cm RMSE survey vertical-accuracy statement as an uncertainty guard, not as guaranteed point error.

rows.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
rows.check: Keep DTM and DSM semantics separate: DTM removes surface objects while DSM includes buildings, vegetation and other objects.

rows.source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
rows.check: Do not promote an official parcel height-difference row until boundary geometry, survey vintage, tile provenance, CRS/vertical datum and sampled cell evidence are all present.
